historical_references.reference: Christina of Sweden, also known as Christina of Denmark, was the queen of Sweden from 1632 to 1654. Born in Denmark, she was the eldest daughter of King Christian IV of Denmark and Norway and Anne Catherine of Brandenburg. She became queen of Sweden at the age of 6, after her father arranged her marriage to King Gustavus Adolphus of Sweden. Christina was known for her intelligence, patronage of the arts, and religious conversions to Catholicism. In 1654, she abdicated the throne and retired from public life to Rome, where she died in 1689.

Christina the Astonishing, also known as Christina Mirabilis, was a Flemish mystic who lived from approximately 1150 to 1224. According to her hagiography, she was born in the village of Den Dungen, near Bruges, to a noble family. After experiencing a series of mystical experiences, she left her family and lived as a hermit, performing various acts of self-mortification and other pious deeds. She was known for her ecstatic experiences, levitation, and ability to heal the sick. Christina's cult was popular in the Low Countries and France, and she was canonized in 1443.
